The first hour or so in the game is great, adding survival, pve, and base building elements to the pokemon format seems like an incredible idea. The map is massive and there are soooo many things you can craft and build. However the crafting is painfully slow, to build a sword literally took 20 minutes of holding the F key, and mamy other items also take painfully long. Even with your pals doing the building for you it is incredibly tedious. The massive map is also incredibly boring, there are very few exciting locations to explore and the bossfights are all fairly underwhelming. The pve is also incredibly boring, while being able to shoot a gun at pals is cool for abit it grows old quiet fast and isnt newrly as compelling as pokemons actual battle mechanics. This game also shamelessly rips off pokemons designs and concepts. Super cool concept and has the potential to be more than pokemon could ever be, but in reality this game is an unimaginitive grindfest that steals all its best traits from other games.

While this might be the best "pokemon-style" game around, the game itself is largely a disappointment. It's a matter of too much and too little at the same time. There might be hundreds of pals, but most of them are elemental variations on pals you've already seen. There might be a huge landmass to discover, but most of it isn't worth taking the time to fully explore. There might be lots of dungeons, but they're only a handful of layouts and skins for them, so it's mostly an exercise in repetition. There's a huge tech tree to explore, but you'll find little reason to actually unlock most of it. By the time my wife and I got through with the world tree stuff, we STILL hadn't tackled many of the summoned boss fights, or the harder tower fights. It's like the progression of this game is all over the place, and at the end all I could think was, "Was my experience what the game designers intended?" because I felt like I was leaving so much of the game unfinished.

I want to start this by being deadass honest with everyone. When I first tried this game, I put 5 hours into it, didn't like it, and didn't look back. 

Then one of my friends kept pestering me to play with them, kept talking about how much they liked it, and I eventually gave in. I'm now 230+ hours deep and this game has no intention of letting me go any time soon. I've been fully engrossed by the optimization that the game offers you for builds and pals, base building feels almost identical to the base building in conan exiles, and I feel the game heavily rewards you for being self sufficient and learning how to play it properly through guides and such. 

All this to say at first, no...I wouldn't have recommended it, now...yes I do, 100%. Especially so if you're neurodivergent and want a super deep system of optimization and build customization to sink your teeth into.

Palworld has been a lot of fun, and I can honestly recommend it if it seems like something you'd enjoy! Base building and crafting are cool, the world is huge and chock-full of stuff (not to mention gorgeous to look at IMO), combat and exploration are fun, and I genuinely love a LOT of the pal designs! It's been a great time, all in all, and the best advice I can give is to not try and play it like a Pokémon game, because it's not supposed to be one - It's meant to be Ark survival.
If you're worried about AI, it's understandable, but I can attest that I haven't found a lick of evidence to ANY AI use in the game or otherwise. The designs look perfectly fine and honestly quite creative to me, and there haven't really been any wonky textures aside from a few low-res cliffs here and there , which kinda just seems more of a graphics thing. And, given how mod-able the game is and the fact that I haven't crashed once, I highly doubt there's any AI in the code either (though I wish I could say the same for a number of workshop mods). And, on top of that, Pocketpair has been strictly non-AI, the only use-case being some art game made by 2 guys at the company, which soon got abandoned and led to their current "No AI" policy.
Overall, I've really enjoyed the game, both before and after 1.0, so if you like base building, exploration, and cool creatures, I'd say give it a shot!

There is so much I love about Palworld.

It’s a complete one-time purchase without the relentless live-service grind—no forced daily chores, time gates, or paywalls blocking features - I’m so tired of that model. You just buy it and play at your own pace.

The world customization is awesome. You can tweak almost every server setting and difficulty slider across different worlds, whether you want a relaxed experience or a brutal survival challenge.

Best of all, I was able to host a dedicated server for my family and friends so we can enjoy the game together.

P.S. To the die-hard Pokémon fans getting salty: a complete lack of competition is the exact reason Nintendo keeps giving you less for more. When there's no rival pushing them, you end up paying full price for mediocre releases. Palworld raising the bar is a good thing.
